$note: Build sheet for Nod on Railway, upstream n8n-io/nod at the pinned tag in NOD_VERSION (nod-v0.9.0, Apache-2.0). Upstream self-host runs server + Postgres + workspace + browser + a filtered Docker-socket proxy + an iptables workspace firewall, and the server reaches workspace and browser ONLY through docker exec (upstream src/providers/docker/command.ts, src/providers/container-browser/index.ts). Railway has no Docker socket, no NET_ADMIN, and one volume per service, so this template: (1) replaces the docker CLI in the server image with relay/docker, a shim that forwards exactly the two exec shapes the server issues to a relay agent on the matching service, over the private network; (2) runs relay/nod-relay-agent.mjs as root in Workspace and Browser — it checks a shared token, applies the same allow rules as upstream's docker-proxy.mjs, and drops privileges with setpriv (groups cleared, no-new-privs, empty capability bounding set) into a scrubbed environment; (3) gives the workspace's two upstream volumes (/workspace and /home/node) one Railway volume via a /home/node symlink into /workspace/.nod-home, so installed tools persist. All server-to-workspace file operations already travel over exec stdio upstream, so no shared volume is needed. Lost vs upstream: the workspace egress firewall (needs NET_ADMIN, which Railway does not grant), so workspace commands can reach the project's private network — dedicate the project to Nod and keep every service token- or password-protected, as this template does. Images are built by .github/workflows/images.yml from upstream's own Dockerfiles at the pinned tag; upstream publishes no images.
name: Nod

source.$note: Upstream Dockerfile.browser (Chromium under Xvfb, agent-browser worker) + relay agent. Sign-ins the agent makes persist in /data on the volume.

NOD_RELAY_TOKEN.description: Shared secret with the Nod server.

deploy.$note: No healthcheckPath, deliberately: Nod returns 403 for any Host other than NOD_PUBLIC_URL's (upstream src/server/access.ts) and /api/health requires the bearer token, so Railway's healthcheck prober can never pass. Restart on failure covers a server that boots before Postgres is ready.

source.$note: Upstream deployment/self-host/Dockerfile + relay/docker shim + images/server-entry.sh (prepares the volume, derives NOD_VAULT_KEY from the seed, writes the relay config, unsets both secrets, drops to node).

BROWSER_CONTAINER.description: Container name the docker shim maps to the Browser relay.

NOD_ANALYTICS_ENABLED.description: Product analytics to n8n. Off, matching upstream self-host.

NOD_AUTH_TOKEN.description: Access token for the web app and desktop app. Paste it into the sign-in form. Must be 43+ letters, digits, - or _. Treat it like a password: it grants full access to the assistant and its connected accounts.

NOD_BROWSER_RELAY.description: Private address of the Browser relay.

NOD_HOST.$note: Dual-stack listen: Railway's edge and private network dial IPv6.

NOD_PUBLIC_URL.description: Exact public origin of the app. Nod rejects requests for any other host, so this is pre-wired to the Railway domain; update it if you attach a custom domain.

NOD_RELAY_TOKEN.description: Shared secret between the Nod server and its Workspace and Browser relays. Generated at deploy time; never leaves the project's private network.

NOD_VAULT_SEED.$note: Nod needs NOD_VAULT_KEY as canonical base64 of exactly 32 bytes (upstream src/providers/environment/key-store.ts), which secret() cannot emit; images/server-entry.sh derives it as base64(sha256(seed)) at boot. Setting NOD_VAULT_KEY directly overrides the seed.
NOD_VAULT_SEED.description: Seed for the Vault encryption key. Back it up somewhere safe: saved credentials cannot be decrypted without it, and a database backup alone cannot recover them.

NOD_WORKSPACE_RELAY.description: Private address of the Workspace relay.

WORKSPACE_CONTAINER.description: Container name the docker shim maps to the Workspace relay.

source.$note: Railway's own Postgres image, the :18 line — the same image Railway's official Postgres template deploys (PostgreSQL 18). Upstream Nod pins Postgres 17, but Nod needs no extensions and no version-specific features (gen_random_uuid is core since PG13), so this template ships the current Railway line and its live deploy test verifies Nod against 18 end to end.

PGDATA.description: Data directory inside the volume (Railway volumes ship a lost+found directory at the root).

POSTGRES_PASSWORD.description: Database password. Generated at deploy time.

source.$note: Upstream Dockerfile.workspace (Python, Node, LibreOffice, ffmpeg, OCR) + relay agent. The single volume at /workspace also holds /home/node via symlink, so tools the agent installs persist across restarts and redeploys.

NOD_RELAY_TOKEN.description: Shared secret with the Nod server.
